title: Privacy-focused AI Startup Maple Raises $5.3 Million and Launches AI Desktop Agent
excerpt: Privacy-preserving AI startup Maple recently closed a $5.3 million seed round, formally accelerating its expansion into the personal and enterprise AI agent mar
content_html:
Privacy-preserving AI startup Maple recently closed a $5.3 million seed round, formally accelerating its expansion into the personal and enterprise AI agent market. The round was led by Epic Ventures, with participation from Draper Associates, Planetary VC, and Epoch VC. Maple plans to use the funds to develop a cloud-based AI assistant that can continue executing tasks after the user’s computer is turned off, and it plans to launch a Series A round in the first half of 2027.

Maple was co-founded by former Apple engineer Mark Suman and co-founder and CTO Anthony Ronning. The company’s core strategy is to use technical architecture to ensure that user data cannot be directly accessed by the platform, rather than relying solely on privacy policy promises. It uses trusted execution environments (TEEs) and end-to-end encryption. User data is encrypted locally before entering the TEE for processing, and after AI inference is completed, it is encrypted again before being returned. The company says that even if the system is hacked or receives a government request for data, it cannot directly provide users’ original data.

On the product side, Maple offers an AI chat app that supports open-source models such as DeepSeek, Kimi, GLM, Gemma, and OpenAI GPT-OSS. The newly launched desktop app Maple Work further features computer control, file processing, browser operation, and application integration capabilities. It can connect to services such as Gmail and Calendar, and supports collaborating with AI tools such as Claude and Codex to execute tasks.

Maple plans to enter the enterprise market in 2027 through pilot projects and launch a zero-data-retention solution. It is currently pursuing SOC 2 compliance certification and security audits. The company disclosed that its number of registered customers grew 60-fold over the past three months. Maple currently uses a subscription model: the Pro plan costs $20 per month, while the Max plans cost $100 and $200 per month, respectively. The company is headquartered in Austin and San Francisco, and its current team has about 4 people.
